title: Horton Tech partnership lane - outreach + pilot notes
content:
Quick context: Horton Tech (mid-market, fintech-adjacent retail analytics) — builds fraud/loyalty signals and merchant performance dashboards. Heard via inbound lead (marketing webinar) — appears to be exploring LLMs for: (1) conversational merchant support, (2) automated insights from transaction streams, (3) embeddings for similarity search across merchant profiles.

Account snapshot (notes to self):
- HQ: Austin, ~220 employees, Series B (2023) — strong engineering org but no large infra footprint.
- CTO: Priya Raman (ex-payments). Head of Data: Marcus Li. Product lead for Insights: Diego Alvarez.
- Tech signals: uses Snowflake + Redpanda for event ingestion, model experimentation on small in-house GPU infra (occasional EC2 p3). GitHub public infra repo with data pipelines. Mentions using OpenAI in a few tickets (trial).
- Potential fit: Redwood Hosted API for quick PoC -> Dedicated for predictable throughput if embeddings/predict pipelines expand -> Private if regulatory customers require VPC.

Why this could move:
- Use cases align with Redwood strengths: throughput-sensitive embeddings + streaming chat for merchant-facing tool.
- They care about unit cost — CFO flagged model spend during Q4 (marketing webinar comment).
- Decision window: product roadmap mentions an "AI insights pilot" for H2; potential pilot starting Q3 if budget approves.

Unknowns / questions to validate early:
- Data residency or HIPAA/PCI constraints? (likely not PCI on our side but merchants' data could be sensitive)
- Expected QPS for chat/embedding queries? (estimate: 5-20 qps if rolled to 50k merchants)
- SLA expectations for latency — do they need sub-200ms for chats? maybe 300-500ms is acceptable.
- Which models are they experimenting with (open vs proprietary)?

Quick outreach play (sequence + templates):
1) LinkedIn + short email segue (day 0)
- LI note: "Hi Priya — enjoyed your paneI at RetailAI Summit. Small idea on reducing inference spend while keeping response times competitive, would love 10 mins to share a few cost/latency tradeoffs we saw with other analytics platforms. — Maya"
- Email subject options: (A) "Quick idea to cut inference spend for Horton" (B) "Pilot idea: merchant insights + predictable latency"
- Email body (short):
  Hi Priya —

  Saw your RetailAI Summit talk — congrats on the product roadmap. We work with analytics/platform teams to cut per-embedding / per-token costs while keeping latency predictable (Redwood Inference). Two quick notes: 1) we can suggest quantization + batching profiles that reduce token cost by ~30% for typical merchant prompts, 2) we support a path from hosted API -> dedicated capacity to avoid surprises as you scale. Would you be open to 15 mins next week for a quick idea share?

  Cheers,
  Maya

2) Follow-up (day 3) — add a one-pager link + suggested time slots.
3) If no reply, send a short case study (day 7) showing a similar analytics startup reduced inference spend by 28% after switching to Redwood Dedicated.

Cold call opener / discovery script (4–6 min):
- Intro: "Maya from Redwood — we help analytics teams lower inference cost while keeping latency consistent. Quick Q: are you currently measuring per-call token spend and seeing surprises in Q4?"
- Discovery bullets: "What are your top 2 inference workloads? (chat / embeddings / rerank). How many unique merchants or MAUs do you expect in 12 months? Any hard latency SLOs?"
- Value hook: "We can model a 90-day pilot that shows cost-per-embedding and tail-latency improvements with clear rollback paths."

Objection handling (common ones + quick rebuttals):
- "We already use OpenAI / vendor X": 
  Rebuttal: "Great — many customers use OpenAI for dev. For production, they add a dedicated layer for predictable latency/cost. We can sit behind your existing workflows and show delta vs status quo in a short pilot."
- "We don’t have the budget":
  Rebuttal: "Pilot can be scoped as a technical evaluation (no upfront platform fees) — we often run a 30–90 day pilot where we track unit economics and operational impact before procurement."
- "We are worried about data privacy":
  Rebuttal: "We offer Private deployments and can sign tighter DPA/KMS controls; for most pilots we can use token redaction + ephemeral keys to reduce exposure."
- "We can build this ourselves":
  Rebuttal: "Totally reasonable — the question is runway. We’ve seen internal builds incur hidden ops costs (kernel tuning, KV cache, rolling upgrades). We can show a TCO comparison for your expected QPS in the pilot phase."

Pilot / proposal sketch (for SDR -> AE handoff):
- Goals: validate latency SLOs for merchant chat (95th < 400ms), show embedding similarity recall >= baseline, demonstrate 20–30% reduction in per-embedding and per-token cost via batching/quantization.
- Scope: 4-week technical pilot: 2 weeks onboarding (credentials, sample dataset, baseline measurements), 2 weeks optimization and A/B testing.
- Deliverables: latency/cost baseline report, recommended config (batch sizes, quant profiles), short tech transfer doc for devops.
- Success criteria (pass->advance to paid pilot): measurable cost delta + no-major-regressions in recall/quality on a held-out prompt set.
- Pricing flavor: metered hosted for initial pilot (credits), recommend Dedicated once qps > threshold X (tbd after baseline).

Internal notes / to-dos (assignments):
- Rafi: try to find any public job postings mentioning ML infra to estimate infra maturity (due 2026-01-20).
- Liz: build short one-pager (2 slides) comparing hosted vs dedicated for embeddings at scale (due 2026-01-22).
- Maya: intro email + LI message (send by 2026-01-18).

Pitching hooks / technical anecdotes to use live:
- "We helped a payments analytics customer move embeddings to a quantized variant and saved them ~30% in token-equivalent spend without quality hit using our Evaluate+rollout hooks."
- "Prefix cache + dynamic batching cut tail latencies on bursty merchant queries by half in one customer pilot."

Risks / red flags:
- Could be very price-sensitive; procurement cycle might stretch if no clear ROI.
- If they prefer closed-source LLM vendors only — need to check model preferences early.

Next steps (short):
1) Send intro to Priya + attach 1-pager (by Maya).
2) Rafi to post a brief Recon note in the sales workspace with topline technical signals.
3) If reply -> schedule 15-min discovery with product lead Diego.

Scratch + brain dump:
- consider an A/B test variant: (A) Redwood-hosted + model quantization vs (B) existing vendor with caching proxies. Measure 95th latency and cost per 1k embeddings.
- Short checklist to ask in discovery: data flows (are merchant transaction ids hashed?), compliance constraints, expected retention of embeddings, offline retrain cadence.

Random reminders to self:
- Keep outreach short. Avoid heavy ROI math until we have QPS estimates.
- Use the case study of "payments analytics startup" — swap in pronouns & numbers to make it feel bespoke.
- If they ping for SSO/KMS questions, loop in security@redwood early.

End of notes.

-- Maya
(rough, shareable once Liz adds one-pager)
